notes:
Read-along now remembers what it read.

Working out what a page says is slow and imperfect, and until now the answer was thrown away when you closed the app — so every re-read paid for it again, and every mistake came back identically. It is kept now. Coming back to a chapter is instant, and a page it got wrong can eventually be corrected once and stay corrected.

Alongside that, three faults found by reviewing the change before shipping it:

Every page turn had two pages being read at once from the same three temporary files, because the files were named after the slice and not the page. A page could be narrated with the next page's dialogue, or quietly fall back to the blurry whole-page reading that slicing exists to replace.

A balloon of a single word — "WHAT?!", "HUH?" — was never recognised as a repeat, so any of them near a slice join was read out twice. The commonest balloon in comics was the one exempt from the check.

And a remembered page had no way back. Reader settings now has "Forget this chapter", and anything remembered by an older version is re-read rather than trusted.
